CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Broccoli — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches broccoli the way children already see it — as little trees — and uses matching to train careful looking.

What is this?

Broccoli is a green vegetable grown for its flower buds, eaten before they open. The thick stalk holds up a crown of bumpy florets that look exactly like a tiny tree.

What does it mean?

Match the broccoli asks the child to find two of the same — same shape, same color, same tree. Matching is the toddler version of sorting, and sorting is the root of math.

What does the child need to know?

The tree story is not a trick; it is a handle. Children who call broccoli a tree eat more of it, and the botany catches up later — the florets really are buds.

Why this matters

Green vegetables are the shelf’s hardest sell and its biggest prize; giving the child a game instead of a lecture changes the whole negotiation.

What it teaches

Same-and-different spotting, the word tree as a shape handle, and brave-bite courage.

Words to learn

broccolitreegreenmatchfloretcrunchy

Say this to your child

“Broccoli! A little tree on a trunk. Make your hand be a tree — fingers up! Now find the matching tree... under which cup? Lift it slow... there it is!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and trace the tree with a finger — trunk, then bumpy leaves. Ask the child to hold up a hand-tree: fingers up, arm the trunk. Then hide a second broccoli card or picture under a cup and play match-the-tree until the crown is found. Any real broccoli at the table earns one brave bite, dips allowed.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the matching, not the eating. A child who matches perfectly but skips the bite is winning the lesson; the bites follow on their own schedule.

Ask your child

What does broccoli look like? Where is the trunk? Can you find the matching tree? What color is the tree?

What your child can say or do

Tree! / Little trees. / Match it! / Green one.

Out in the real world

Broccoli rides every salad bar and kids’ menu — the tree handle travels to restaurants, grandma’s table and the freezer aisle without any re-teaching.

Try it together

Forest walk: line up five vegetable cards like trees and let a toy animal walk the forest, stopping to sniff each tree — the broccoli tree gets the longest sniff.

Understanding check

Mix the broccoli card into three other food cards and ask the child to find the tree. One correct grab — tree declared or not — passes.

This lesson pairs with the Broccoli flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
